schemes.definition: A software application, program, plugin, utility, or suite developed to perform specific computing tasks or services.
System software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides common services for computer programs.
An organization or commercial enterprise that develops, manufactures, or distributes software products and technology services.
A flaw, bug, or weakness in a system or software that can be exploited by an attacker.
A web address that specifies the location of a resource on a computer network and the mechanism for retrieving it.
A distinct territorial body or sovereign state with its own government, borders, and population.
A public sector authority, ministry, department, or agency established by a state to perform specific administrative or regulatory functions.
A formal public notice published by a vendor or organization detailing security vulnerabilities, risks, and remediation measures for software or hardware.
An individual human being, such as a government official, cybersecurity expert, researcher, or public figure.
A commercial business enterprise, corporation, or non-governmental firm providing goods or services.
A commercial organization that provides cybersecurity products, threat intelligence, security research, or information security services.
A digital file crafted, modified, or distributed by threat actors to execute attacks, deliver malware, or compromise systems.
A unique numerical identifier assigned to a device or network endpoint communicating over the Internet Protocol.
A unique identifier for an electronic mail account used to send and receive digital messages across a computer network.
A text-based identifier used to name and locate network resources and computers connected to the internet.
A distinct group, variant, or category of malicious software sharing common code, behavior, or operational characteristics.
A modular part, library, subsystem, or service integrated within a larger software application or operating system.
An intergovernmental or transnational body established by treaty or agreement among multiple sovereign states.
An individual, group, or organization that conducts malicious cyber activities, attacks, or espionage campaigns against target systems.
A formal system of rules, syntax, and symbols used to write instructions and computer programs for software execution.
An organization that provides computing infrastructure, server capacity, cloud services, or web hosting services to customers.
An online platform or service that facilitates social networking, user communication, and content sharing.
A state-authorized armed force, defense body, or military unit tasked with national defense and warfare operations.
An internet-hosted platform or application providing specific functionality, APIs, or digital services to users over a network.
An organization or team responsible for analyzing, handling, and responding to computer security incidents and cyber threats.
A non-profit, citizen-based organization that operates independently of government to address social, political, educational, or humanitarian issues.
An account, channel, or profile on a social networking or messaging platform used to publish content and communicate with users.
A specialized overlay network or routing system designed to enable private and anonymous communication over the internet.
A database entry or path in an operating system registry used to store configuration settings, application data, or system options.
A platform, organization, or infrastructure providing electronic mail transmission, hosting, and webmail services to users.
A connected group of IP routing prefixes managed by network operators with a single, clearly defined routing policy.
An enterprise or organization that provides telecommunications, mobile network, voice, or internet connectivity services.
A digital service or application that enables real-time text, voice, or multimedia messaging and communication between users over the internet.
An operating system configuration configured to automatically execute a script, program, or command at specified times or system events.
